title: Commercial auto
summary: Commercial auto forms, Business Auto covered auto symbols, key liability and physical damage rules, garagekeepers, endorsements and federal truck minimums.
objectives: Match each commercial auto form to the business it fits
Read the Business Auto covered auto symbols
Tell the three garagekeepers bases apart
Know the key endorsements, including Michigan PIP and PPI

scenes.title: Commercial auto
scenes.subtitle: Business auto forms, covered auto symbols, garagekeepers, endorsements and federal truck limits

beats.text: Businesses insure their vehicles on commercial auto forms. The Business Auto numbers here come from its 2020 edition.
beats.say: Businesses insure their vehicles on commercial auto forms. The Business Auto numbers here come from its twenty twenty edition.

scenes.title: The commercial auto forms
items: Hauling property by auto for hire

beats.text: The Business Auto form has five sections: covered autos, liability, physical damage, conditions and definitions.
beats.say: The Business Auto form has five sections: covered autos, liability, physical damage, conditions and definitions.

beats.text: The Garage form combined liability, garagekeepers and physical damage for garage risks. The Business Auto Physical Damage form gave physical damage only. Both were eliminated in the 2013 revision.
beats.say: The Garage form combined liability, garagekeepers and physical damage for garage risks. The Business Auto Physical Damage form gave physical damage only. Both were eliminated in the twenty thirteen revision.

beats.text: The Truckers form is for those hauling property by auto for hire. The Motor Carrier form is broader: it fits both for-hire carriers and private carriers hauling their own goods.
beats.say: The Truckers form is for those hauling property by auto for hire. The Motor Carrier form is broader: it fits both for-hire carriers and private carriers hauling their own goods.

scenes.title: Covered auto symbols (2020 Business Auto)
items: Owned autos, by type or by law
Mobile equipment subject to auto laws

beats.text: Covered auto symbols show which autos get each coverage. Symbol 1 is any auto.
beats.say: Covered auto symbols show which autos get each coverage. Symbol one is any auto.

beats.text: 2 through 6 are owned autos: 2 all owned, 3 private passenger, 4 other than private passenger, 5 those subject to no-fault, and 6 those subject to a compulsory uninsured motorists law.
beats.say: Two through six are owned autos: two all owned, three private passenger, four other than private passenger, five those subject to no-fault, and six those subject to a compulsory uninsured motorists law.

beats.text: 7 is specifically described autos. A new auto is covered only if you already cover all owned autos for that coverage, or it's a replacement, and you tell the insurer within 30 days. Symbols 1 to 6 and 19 cover new autos automatically.
beats.say: Seven is specifically described autos. A new auto is covered only if you already cover all owned autos for that coverage, or it's a replacement, and you tell the insurer within thirty days. Symbols one to six and nineteen cover new autos automatically.

beats.text: 8 is hired autos, but not ones borrowed from your employees. 9 is non-owned autos, including employees' own cars used in your business. 19 is mobile equipment subject to a compulsory or financial responsibility law.
beats.say: Eight is hired autos, but not ones borrowed from your employees. Nine is non-owned autos, including employees' own cars used in your business. Nineteen is mobile equipment subject to a compulsory or financial responsibility law.

scenes.q: A business wants liability coverage for employees' personal cars when they run company errands. Which Business Auto symbol applies?
scenes.why: Symbol 9 covers autos you don't own, lease, hire, rent or borrow that are used in your business, including employees' cars. Symbol 8 excludes autos borrowed from employees.

beats.text: Quick check. A business wants liability coverage for employees' personal cars used on company errands. Which symbol applies? Pick an answer.
beats.say: Quick check. A business wants liability coverage for employees' personal cars used on company errands. Which symbol applies? Pick an answer.

reveal.text: The answer is symbol 9, non-owned autos. Symbol 8, hired autos, leaves out autos borrowed from employees.
reveal.say: The answer is symbol nine, non-owned autos. Symbol eight, hired autos, leaves out autos borrowed from employees.

scenes.title: Business Auto liability: key rules
scenes.src: CA 00 01 11 20, Sections II.A.2.a, II.B.6, II.B.8, IV.B.5

items.label: Bail bonds up to $2,000
items.detail: Lost earnings up to $250 a day. The personal auto policy's bail limit is $250

items.label: Care, custody or control
items.detail: Excludes property owned or transported by the insured, like cargo

items.label: Mechanical devices
items.detail: Excluded unless the device is attached to the auto, or is a hand truck

items.label: Other insurance
items.detail: Primary for owned autos, excess for non-owned autos

beats.text: Liability supplementary payments include bail bonds up to $2,000, and lost earnings up to $250 a day. Don't mix that up with the personal auto policy's bail limit of $250.
beats.say: Liability supplementary payments include bail bonds up to two thousand dollars, and lost earnings up to two hundred fifty dollars a day. Don't mix that up with the personal auto policy's bail limit of two hundred fifty dollars.

beats.text: Two exclusions to know. Care, custody or control excludes property you own or transport, like packages in your van. And injury from moving property with a mechanical device is excluded, unless the device is attached to the covered auto.
beats.say: Two exclusions to know. Care, custody or control excludes property you own or transport, like packages in your van. And injury from moving property with a mechanical device is excluded, unless the device is attached to the covered auto.

beats.text: Other insurance: the form is primary for autos you own, and excess for autos you don't.
beats.say: Other insurance: the form is primary for autos you own, and excess for autos you don't.

scenes.title: Business Auto physical damage

columns.name: Specified Causes of Loss
points: Sinking, burning, collision or derailment of a conveyance carrying it

columns.name: Collision
points: Hitting an object, like a guardrail
Glass broken in a collision, if you choose

scenes.tell: Specified causes is a short named list. It doesn't include hitting a deer or glass breakage.

beats.text: Physical damage comes in three coverages. Comprehensive includes glass breakage, hitting a bird or animal, and falling objects.
beats.say: Physical damage comes in three coverages. Comprehensive includes glass breakage, hitting a bird or animal, and falling objects.

beats.text: Specified Causes of Loss is a named list: fire, lightning, explosion, theft, windstorm, hail, earthquake, flood, vandalism, and damage to a conveyance carrying the auto.
beats.say: Specified Causes of Loss is a named list: fire, lightning, explosion, theft, windstorm, hail, earthquake, flood, vandalism, and damage to a conveyance carrying the auto.

beats.text: Collision pays for hitting an object. So a van with only specified causes is covered for a flood, but not for hitting a deer.
beats.say: Collision pays for hitting an object. So a van with only specified causes is covered for a flood, but not for hitting a deer.

scenes.title: Garagekeepers: three ways to pay
scenes.story: Hail damages a customer's car while it sits at a repair shop for service. The shop carries garagekeepers Comprehensive and did nothing wrong. Which garagekeepers basis pays, and when?

items.label: Legal liability
items.detail: Pays only if the shop is legally liable, so it pays nothing here

items.label: Direct excess
items.detail: Pays regardless of liability, but excess over the customer's own insurance

items.label: Direct primary
items.detail: Pays regardless of liability, as primary

scenes.answer: Direct excess or direct primary pays. Only direct primary pays first, before the customer's own insurance.

beats.text: Garagekeepers covers customers' autos left in your care while you service, repair, park or store them. Hail hits a customer's car at a repair shop with garagekeepers Comprehensive. The shop did nothing wrong. Does it pay?
beats.say: Garagekeepers covers customers' autos left in your care while you service, repair, park or store them. Hail hits a customer's car at a repair shop with garagekeepers Comprehensive. The shop did nothing wrong. Does it pay?

beats.text: It depends on the basis. Legal liability, the default, pays only if the shop is legally liable. So here, nothing.
beats.say: It depends on the basis. Legal liability, the default, pays only if the shop is legally liable. So here, nothing.

beats.text: Direct excess pays regardless of liability, but only over the customer's own insurance. Direct primary pays regardless of liability, and pays first.
beats.say: Direct excess pays regardless of liability, but only over the customer's own insurance. Direct primary pays regardless of liability, and pays first.

scenes.title: Auto or mobile equipment?

columns.name: Mobile equipment
points: Vehicles used solely on or next to your premises

columns.name: Auto
points: Self-propelled with snow-removal, road-maintenance or street-cleaning gear
Cherry pickers on an auto or truck chassis
Any land vehicle subject to a compulsory or FR law

scenes.tell: Unendorsed, Business Auto covers mobile equipment for liability only while a covered auto carries or tows it.

beats.text: Is it an auto or mobile equipment? Bulldozers, forklifts, farm machinery and crawler-tread vehicles are mobile equipment.
beats.say: Is it an auto or mobile equipment? Bulldozers, forklifts, farm machinery and crawler-tread vehicles are mobile equipment.

beats.text: But a self-propelled vehicle with permanently attached snow-removal, road-maintenance or street-cleaning equipment is an auto. So is any land vehicle subject to a compulsory or financial responsibility law.
beats.say: But a self-propelled vehicle with permanently attached snow-removal, road-maintenance or street-cleaning equipment is an auto. So is any land vehicle subject to a compulsory or financial responsibility law.

beats.text: Without an endorsement, the Business Auto form covers mobile equipment for liability only while a covered auto carries or tows it.
beats.say: Without an endorsement, the Business Auto form covers mobile equipment for liability only while a covered auto carries or tows it.

scenes.title: Key commercial auto endorsements
scenes.src: CA 99 10 (IRMI); CA 99 17 (summaries); CA 20 01 11 20; CA 20 15 (FC&S, Rough Notes); CA 22 20; CA 22 24

items.label: Drive Other Car
items.detail: Non-owned auto coverage for a named person, like an executive with a company car

items.label: Individual Named Insured
items.detail: For a sole proprietor: personal-auto-type coverage for the individual and family

items.label: Lessor additional insured
items.detail: The lessor becomes an insured; the leased auto counts as one you own

items.label: Mobile Equipment
items.detail: Scheduled vehicles become covered autos, but not for operating their machinery

items.label: Michigan PIP and PPI
items.detail: Add no-fault benefits; symbol 5 marks owned autos subject to no-fault

beats.text: Now endorsements. Drive Other Car gives a named person, like an executive with a company car and no personal policy, non-owned auto coverage like a personal auto policy.
beats.say: Now endorsements. Drive Other Car gives a named person, like an executive with a company car and no personal policy, non-owned auto coverage like a personal auto policy.

beats.text: Individual Named Insured is for an individual, like a sole proprietor. It adds personal-auto-type coverage for that person and family members.
beats.say: Individual Named Insured is for an individual, like a sole proprietor. It adds personal-auto-type coverage for that person and family members.

beats.text: The lessor endorsement makes the leasing company an insured, and treats a scheduled leased auto as one you own. The Mobile Equipment endorsement treats scheduled vehicles as covered autos, but liability excludes operating their attached machinery.
beats.say: The lessor endorsement makes the leasing company an insured, and treats a scheduled leased auto as one you own. The Mobile Equipment endorsement treats scheduled vehicles as covered autos, but liability excludes operating their attached machinery.

beats.text: The Business Auto form has no PIP section. In Michigan, PIP and PPI endorsements add those benefits. Symbol 5 means owned autos subject to no-fault.
beats.say: The Business Auto form has no P I P section. In Michigan, P I P and P P I endorsements add those benefits. Symbol five means owned autos subject to no-fault.

scenes.q: A Michigan plumbing company insures its vans under the 2020 Business Auto Coverage Form. Its Michigan no-fault PIP is provided by:
choices: A Michigan Personal Injury Protection endorsement
scenes.why: The Business Auto form has no PIP section. ISO's Michigan Personal Injury Protection endorsement adds the PIP that Michigan's no-fault law requires.

beats.text: Your turn. A Michigan plumbing company insures its vans on the Business Auto form. What provides its Michigan no-fault PIP? Pick an answer.
beats.say: Your turn. A Michigan plumbing company insures its vans on the Business Auto form. What provides its Michigan no-fault P I P? Pick an answer.

reveal.text: The answer is a Michigan Personal Injury Protection endorsement. The Business Auto form itself has no PIP section.
reveal.say: The answer is a Michigan Personal Injury Protection endorsement. The Business Auto form itself has no P I P section.

scenes.title: Motor Carrier Act of 1980: federal minimums

items.label: For-hire, nonhazardous, GVWR 10,001 lbs or more

beats.text: Finally, federal rules under the Motor Carrier Act of 1980. A for-hire interstate carrier hauling nonhazardous property in vehicles of 10,001 pounds or more needs at least $750,000.
beats.say: Finally, federal rules under the Motor Carrier Act of nineteen eighty. A for-hire interstate carrier hauling nonhazardous property in vehicles of ten thousand one pounds or more needs at least seven hundred fifty thousand dollars.

beats.text: Oil and most hazardous materials need $1 million. Certain bulk hazardous substances, explosives and radioactive materials need $5 million. Proof is the MCS-90 endorsement.
beats.say: Oil and most hazardous materials need one million dollars. Certain bulk hazardous substances, explosives and radioactive materials need five million dollars. Proof is the M C S ninety endorsement.
